subject: Operations
title: The Inca Quipu System
description: A quick, practical guide to The Inca Quipu System.

hook.text: The Inca Empire had no written language yet managed millions of people across 4,000 km of mountains.

buildup.text: They used quipus—knotted strings of different colors and lengths to record data precisely.

discovery.text: Quipus tracked census data, tax records, and inventory. Knot positions encoded numbers.

twist.text: Spanish conquerors destroyed most quipus. Only about 600 survive, and many remain undeciphered.

climax.text: The Incas proved you don't need writing to run an empire—just a reliable data system.

punchline.text: Knots on a string managed an empire.

quiz.question: What were quipus used for in the Inca Empire?
options: Recording data like inventory and census
